method: File-only source/diff review, AST parsing without importing or executing the controller, and SHA256 reads of the six exact existing cached launcher/binary/runtime-profile files. No process inspection, listener probe, signal, network, database command, retention, native stop, browser, or Chrome action was performed by reviewer.
reviewedDelta: Auth and PostgREST keep their same exact PID/UID/start/cwd/listener targets while the command marker is bound to the official .auth-wrapped/.postgrest-wrapped executable instead of its shell launcher.
Each of those services additionally requires exact SHA256 of its existing launcher, wrapped binary, and .runtime-env.sh before target identification. All six pinned files match their existing bytes.

Identification requires lsof txt to map the exact resolved wrapped executable. The existing start-time, current-user, working-directory, exact loopback listener and command-marker checks remain in force at initial identification and immediately before each SIGTERM.

The same nine task-owned target PID/port sets, absent-only-if-port-free rule, SIGTERM-only behavior, bounded wait, explicit root release gate, and refusal to use stronger/broad signals remain unchanged.

The final retainer and plan are byte-identical to their previously reviewed pins. Retention still requires the exact nine-process stop report and absent listeners before snapshot/dump validation, and native stops require their separate final gate.

resolvedPreExecutionFinding.issue: The wrapper-material map reused the name expected, overwriting the service PID/port map and causing the next service lookup to fail before target identification or signals.
resolvedPreExecutionFinding.resolution: The author renamed the inner map to wrapped_expected. AST inspection confirms the service expected map is now assigned only once. This resolves the static defect before execution.

limits: Preparation review does not prove that any process is currently owned, listening, stopped, or quiescent; the controller must make and preserve those operational observations after root final release.
No current process configuration was changed by this source-only guard correction, and no new software permission or browser fallback is authorized by this review.
No successful retention, actual restore, hosted recovery, or CNF acceptance follows from this static supplement. Historical review and raw operation reports remain separate.
A further controller, target, launcher, binary, runtime-profile, plan or retainer change requires renewed comparison.
